The regional military rulers who divided China after the death of President Yuan Shikai in 1916. The map uses the label in 1938 for the large part of China not held by Japan.

In the Warlord Era proper, from 1916 to 1928, rival cliques fought for Beijing and the provinces, taxing peasants heavily and buying foreign arms. The Nationalists under Chiang Kai-shek launched the Northern Expedition in 1926 and by 1928 had united the country in name. In practice many warlords simply joined the new government and kept their armies and provinces, such as Yan Xishan in Shanxi and the Guangxi clique in the south.

In 1938, the second year of the Second Sino-Japanese War, Japan held the coast, Manchuria and the main cities. Chiang's government had retreated to Chongqing and depended on these regional strongmen, while Mao Zedong's Communists held the northwest. Only after 1949 did the People's Republic end their power.
sum: The regional military rulers who divided China after the death of President Yuan Shikai in 1916. The map uses the label in 1938 for the large part of China not held by Japan.
